one_sentence_story: Formulated on page 62 of Donald Hebb's 1949 book and proven physiologically via hippocampal Long-Term Potentiation by Tim Bliss and Terje Lømo in 1973, Hebb's Rule ('cells that fire together, wire together' — especially when A fires milliseconds before B) explains how coincident brain activity physically links ideas, habits, and neural networks.
so_what_for_you: Use Hebbian timing on purpose ('Habit Stacking'): trigger a new study or health habit immediately AFTER a rock-solid daily cue (pouring morning coffee) so Cue A reliably fires milliseconds before Action B — and un-pair bad triggers ('out of sync, lose your link').

jargon_map.plain: principle that when Neuron A repeatedly helps fire Neuron B, the synaptic connection from A to B grows stronger
jargon_map.analogy: two hikers walking the same meadow trail together until it packs into a paved path

jargon_map.plain: web of mutually wired neurons representing a concept (e.g., grandmother's voice + face + baking smell) where lighting up 20% ignites the whole web
jargon_map.analogy: a string of holiday lights switched on from any corner

jargon_map.plain: lasting 200%+ strengthening of hippocampal synapses after brief high-frequency co-activation discovered by Bliss & Lømo
jargon_map.analogy: the living physiological proof of Hebb's 1949 guess

jargon_map.plain: molecular coincidence detector that opens ONLY when glutamate arrives from Cell A while Cell B is simultaneously depolarized
jargon_map.analogy: a bank vault requiring two keys turned at the exact same second

jargon_map.plain: millisecond refinement where A-before-B (+15 ms) strengthens the link (LTP) while A-after-B (-15 ms) weakens it (LTD)
